decision: Launch with one series: 'Sky This Week' — weekly, location-specific, computed night-sky guide (vertical short, 40–55 s)
rationale: Best fit of (a) defensible quality: every claim is computed from ephemerides, so we can't drift into slop, (b) recurring demand with natural weekly novelty, (c) monetisation beyond Shorts ads (gear/sponsor fit: Astronomy.com's weekly sky column is Celestron-sponsored), (d) low risk under YouTube's July-2026 'inauthentic content' clarification, which targets repetitive mass-produced content rather than AI-assisted work with original input. Shorts RPM is small for any niche (estimates /usr/bin/zsh.04–1.44 for education), so Shorts are treated as a funnel; long-form and sponsors are the revenue path. Review after 8 published episodes using recorded metrics.
alternatives: General space-facts shorts (rejected: most saturated slop niche, no data moat)
Science/tech news shorts (deferred: needs sourced-facts workflow + speed; good second series once the pipeline is proven)
Long-form explainers first (deferred: higher RPM but far more production per video; reuse templates later)

decision: Imagery policy: real data and real images only (computed sky, NASA/ESA public imagery with credits); AI-generated images off by default, allowed only when labelled and recorded with aiGenerated=true
rationale: User preference; also the channel's whole differentiation is accuracy. AI images of real objects would undermine the 'computed, not made up' promise.

decision: Human approval gate stays on (autoApprove=false); synthetic voice is disclosed on every platform (TikTok video_made_with_ai, description line)
rationale: A wrong date or direction destroys trust in a 'where to look' channel; the gate costs ~5 min/week. Disclosure is honest and avoids policy risk.

decision: Switch package manager from npm to pnpm 12 (packageManager pinned); allow native builds only for esbuild, onnxruntime-node, sharp; deny protobufjs postinstall
rationale: User asked. Strict resolution prevents phantom dependencies, faster installs/CI, pnpm's minimum-release-age gives a supply-chain buffer. Verified: typecheck, lint, 73 tests, Remotion bundle, Kokoro TTS and a Remotion still render all work under pnpm.
alternatives: Stay on npm (works, but looser resolution)
bun (faster, but less mature with Remotion/onnxruntime)

decision: Self-host Postiz from this repo (infra/postiz): official compose adapted with secrets in a gitignored .env, pinned images (postiz-app v2.25.3), ports on 127.0.0.1, Renovate PRs for the stack never automerged
rationale: User requirement (self-hosted, operated by Claude). Pinned tags + Renovate keep it current without surprise upgrades; Temporal/Elasticsearch versions follow upstream postiz-docker-compose for compatibility.

decision: Dependencies on latest versions; exception: TypeScript held at 6.0.x
rationale: typescript-eslint 8.72 (latest) declares peer typescript <6.1.0; TypeScript 7 would break linting. Encoded in renovate.json allowedVersions so it lifts deliberately.
